Quality you can check

A herbal powder is only as good as the lot it comes from. Here is how each lot is handled, the specifications we work to and the documents you receive.

How each lot is handled

Six steps between the raw herb and a sealed, labelled bag.

  1. 1

    Sourcing

    Raw herbs are bought from growers and processing units in the regions where each plant grows best.

  2. 2

    Cleaning and drying

    Stones, stems and foreign matter are removed, and the material is dried until it is shelf-stable.

  3. 3

    Milling and sieving

    Dried material is ground and sieved to an even particle size, typically 60 to 80 mesh.

  4. 4

    Checking

    Every lot is checked for moisture, particle size, colour and aroma. Third-party lab reports are available on request.

  5. 5

    Packing

    Packed in food-grade liners inside 25 kg bags, each labelled with the product, lot number and packing date.

  6. 6

    Shipping

    Trucked from Pune to JNPT (Nhava Sheva) for sea freight, or to Mumbai air cargo, with export documents prepared.

Typical specifications

Limits depend on the product and on the rules of your market. We agree them before you order and confirm them for each lot on the certificate of analysis.

Typical quality parameters
ParameterTypical specificationHow it is checked
Moisture (loss on drying)8% or lessOven drying
Particle size95% passes 60 to 80 meshSieve analysis
Total ash and acid-insoluble ashWithin Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India limitsGravimetric
Total plate count100,000 cfu/g or lessThird-party lab
Yeast and mould1,000 cfu/g or lessThird-party lab
E. coli and SalmonellaAbsentThird-party lab
Heavy metals (Pb, As, Cd, Hg)Within WHO and API limits for herbal materialThird-party lab
Aflatoxins and pesticide residuesTested to the buyer’s market limits on requestThird-party lab

Documents you receive

Prepared for each shipment, so your customs broker and quality team have what they need.

  • Commercial invoice and packing list

    With every shipment.

  • Certificate of analysis (COA)

    For each lot, listing the tested parameters.

  • Phytosanitary certificate

    Issued by India’s plant quarantine authority for plant products.

  • Certificate of origin

    For customs and preferential duty where it applies.

  • Safety data sheet

    On request for each product.

  • Fumigation or other certificates

    Arranged when your country or buyer requires them.

Test before you buy

We send samples of 100 to 250 g per product by international courier, with a specification sheet, so you can test them in your own lab before a first order of 25 kg or more.

Ask for samples

Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia and your market

For herbal powders we work to the identity and purity limits of the Ayurvedic Pharmacopoeia of India. If your market applies stricter limits, for example EU pesticide maximum residue levels, tell us at the enquiry stage and we will test against them.

Send the products, quantities and destination port. We reply within one working day with prices, lead time and freight options.
